Audit complete and all three open decisions resolved by the owner. Deliverable: docs/privacy/data-safety.md - source-backed inventory of all 15 data flows with code line references, SDK verification against the release classpath, per-question Data safety answers with rationale, decision log, and 5 findings (2 filed as pm-a6l.17/.18, 1 as pm-a6l.19).

android:allowBackup set to false in app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml, with the rationale recorded in the manifest itself and as a convention bullet in AGENTS.md so it is not silently re-enabled. Verified: XML parses, and both merged debug and release manifests carry allowBackup=false. lintDebug and assembleDebug pass. Chose the blanket opt-out over granular dataExtractionRules/fullBackupContent because all server-derived data re-syncs on login and downloaded .m4b files would exceed the Auto Backup quota regardless; the only cost is that player settings and theme are not restored on device migration. docs/privacy/data-safety.md finding F1 updated to Fixed.

Verified on a physical Pixel 10 Pro (56151FDCH000L8, Android 17 / API 37) with the AGP 9 toolchain installing via the documented JAVA_HOME=/opt/android-studio/jbr (JBR 25).

:app:installDebug succeeded. App launches, MainActivity focused, no FATAL, no Hilt/Dagger binding failure, no Room/SQLite error; remaining logcat lines are platform noise (cutils-trace, android.xr flag lookup, an SELinux sysfs denial from RenderThread, a benign MediaSessionCompat media-button-receiver warning).

Subsystems the upgrade moved, all confirmed working: Hilt 2.60.1 (DI graph resolves, ViewModels construct), Room 2.8.4 (pageless.db + wal/shm present, cached books and progress render), DataStore with the new @param:ApplicationContext targets (files/datastore/session.preferences_pb intact, session still signed in), Coil over the authed OkHttp client (cover art loads), offline downloads (book listed under Local Books), and WorkManager's Hilt worker factory (job quotas registered in jobscheduler).

Playback, the media notification and foreground-service behaviour were exercised by the owner and reported working as expected.

Bonus verification: 'dumpsys package' reports flags=[ DEBUGGABLE HAS_CODE ALLOW_CLEAR_USER_DATA ] with ALLOW_BACKUP absent, confirming pm-a6l.17's backup opt-out at the OS level.

compileSdk and targetSdk are 36. All 37 Android 16 behaviour changes triaged (see design notes): the app was already compliant on edge-to-edge, predictive back, fixed-rate work and adaptive layouts, and the rest do not apply. API 36 adds no new mediaPlayback or dataSync foreground-service restrictions.

Build verification on JDK 25: ktlintCheck, lintDebug, testDebugUnitTest, assembleDebug and assembleRelease all pass sequentially. Merged debug and release manifests both carry targetSdkVersion=36. Release network policy unchanged - cleartext still forbidden, debug relaxation still confined to the debug source set.

Runtime verification on Android 16 (AVD Pixel_9_Pro, API 36, android-36.1 google_apis_playstore): dumpsys reports minSdk=26 targetSdk=36; app launches clean, Home renders, covers load, edge-to-edge insets correct, predictive-back OnBackInvokedCallback registered at runtime. The owner exercised download, online playback, offline playback, sync and media-notification controls on that emulator - all working.

Also verified on a physical Pixel 10 Pro (Android 17 / API 37) with the same build: installs, launches clean, session preserved, library and downloaded content intact.

Side effect: fixing pm-a6l.17 properly. Lint's DataExtractionRules check revealed that allowBackup=false alone does not disable device-to-device transfers from API 31, so @xml/data_extraction_rules and @xml/backup_rules were added; both backup lint checks are now clean.

Deferred deliberately: Local Network Permission, filed as pm-a6l.20 - currently opt-in and enforced in a later Android release, so not a targetSdk 36 blocker.

Accepted warning: Lint OldTargetApi still fires because AGP 9.3 knows API 37 exists. Targeting 36 is the deliberate choice; it is what Play requires from 31 August 2026.

CI run 31001265731 passed on the push of the 7-commit batch (head 0e806eb), 5m36s, all four gates green: ktlintCheck, lintDebug, testDebugUnitTest, assembleDebug (4x BUILD SUCCESSFUL in the log).

The specific unknown is resolved: android-actions/setup-android@v4 accepts the SDK licences ('Accepting Android SDK licenses', accept-android-sdk-licenses: true), after which AGP auto-provisions the packages it needs. No explicit sdkmanager step was required for build-tools 36.0.0 or platforms;android-36, even though the run included the compileSdk/targetSdk 36 bump. gradle/actions/setup-gradle@v6 handled the Gradle 9.6.1 wrapper without complaint, and JDK 21 remains sufficient (AGP 9 minimum is 17).

Account type: PERSONAL. Created 2026-08 (Play Console does not display a creation date; the authoritative record is the 25 USD registration-fee receipt in the Google payments profile and the registration confirmation email).

Public developer name: Little Box Labs.

No credentials, phone numbers, account ID or recovery details recorded here - only what is already public or non-sensitive.

DOWNSTREAM CONSEQUENCE, now fact rather than assumption: a personal account created after 2023-11-13 cannot access Production or Pre-registration until it has run a closed test with at least 12 testers opted in continuously for 14 days, after which production access must be applied for and reviewed (usually <= 7 days). Verified against Play Console Help 14151465 on 2026-08-22. pm-a6l.13 was written on the assumption of a personal account; that assumption now holds. An organization account would have skipped this gate but requires a real legal entity and a D-U-N-S number, and account type cannot be changed after registration - it would mean a second account, a second fee, re-verification and an app transfer. Not worth it for a hobby project; the closed test is the accepted cost.

Also confirmed for later steps: the publicly shown developer email must be verified by one-time password on Developer account > Contact details, and per-app store listing contact details are set separately under Store settings (pm-a6l.9). The legal address is only displayed for merchant accounts (paid apps or in-app purchases), so a free app with no IAP does not expose it.

App record created in Play Console on 2026-08-22 and confirmed by the owner (dashboard screenshot shows the four-stage setup flow with "0 testers currently opted in").

Locked in at creation: package live.pageless.mobile, app name Pageless, default language English (United States) en-US, type App, price FREE, user-facing contact email little.box.support@pm.me, Developer Program Policies and US export declarations acknowledged, Play App Signing Terms of Service accepted.

Automatic protection was turned OFF at creation. Full reasoning in this issue's notes; the short version is that only the toothless half (installer check) is available to non-partners, it is incompatible with code transparency, and it exists to discourage the non-Play installation paths this project deliberately supports.

Play App Signing: new apps are auto-enrolled with Google-generated quantum-ready keys, so there was no key to select. The Google-held app signing certificate and our upload certificate only become visible on the Play app signing page after the first bundle upload; verifying that the upload certificate matches SHA-256 A8:29:4C:87:...:7C:2A is explicitly part of pm-a6l.12's acceptance, so it is deferred there rather than claimed here.

Acceptance criterion "no test artifact with an unintended package or certificate has claimed the app identity" holds: nothing has been uploaded to any track yet.

Published and live at https://pageless.live/privacy, confirmed by the owner on 2026-08-22. Source of truth is docs/privacy/privacy-policy.md; the page is generated by ~/Nextcloud/dotfiles/VPS/render_privacy_policy.sh into the pageless-docs static site and deployed with push_to_vps.sh. Two rendering defects were found on the live page and fixed: the title appeared twice, because the script stripped pandoc's h1 with a single-line regex while pandoc wraps its output at a column limit and had split the element across two lines - now stripped from the markdown before pandoc, where a heading is always one line; and the body font was system-ui, which on Linux resolves to the visitor's desktop UI font, so the page rendered in monospace for the maintainer and differently for everyone else - now an explicit sans stack, since a public legal page should look the same to every reader.
